basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A route is a directed path through a network; an itinerary is a plan of legs, visits and transfers.
Neither proves movement; actual movement belongs to the journey model.
Candidates, ranking and selection rationale are kept, not just the chosen option.
Routing engines compute routes; this model records them.

may: Register candidate routes and itineraries with constraints.
mustNot: Present a route as legally permitted or safe without evidence.
Book or ticket on behalf of a traveller without consent.
requiresHuman: Selecting routes for hazardous loads or vulnerable travellers.

considerations: Routes for vulnerable travellers must respect accessibility needs.
Routing choices can push traffic into residential areas.

properties.reason: A route is planned geometry and sequence; its length is derived data, not a property of a physical body.

items: A route has ordered waypoints or segments with geometry; an itinerary has ordered legs with times and services.
Often confused with a journey (actual movement), a line (service pattern) and a schedule.
Routes violating restrictions such as weight or height.
